name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Nethanel the scribe. His role is noted within the Levitical context, emphasizing his connection to the priestly tribe. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's attentive nature. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:6 and was not given directly by God but holds significant spiritual meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Shemaiah is explicitly recorded as the son of Nethanel, who was a scribe. Scripture does not mention any other family relationships beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance lies primarily in his Levitical heritage and his identification as the son of Nethanel the scribe, situating him within the priestly lineage responsible for temple duties and the transmission of sacred writings. His mention in 1 Chronicles 24:6 connects him to the organization of priestly divisions, underscoring the continuity of God's covenantal worship through faithful service. This highlights the importance of faithful lineage and scribal roles in maintaining the spiritual life of Israel.
